result:
The city hired its first official listener by mistake.

The job posting was meant to say *local liaison*, but a formatting error removed most of the second word, and by the time anyone noticed, forty-three people had applied.

Mara got the job because she was the only candidate who waited for the interviewer to finish his questions.

Her office was a former supply closet beside the water department. For the first week, people brought her complaints about drains. She wrote them down and took them next door.

In the second week, a man came in carrying a motorcycle helmet.

“There’s nothing wrong with my water,” he said.

“All right.”

He sat down.

“My son bought one of these.”

“A motorcycle?”

The man nodded. For several minutes he turned the helmet in his hands, polishing the visor with his thumb.

Eventually he said, “I used to ride.”

Mara waited.

Word spread slowly. A baker came to explain why he had stopped making wedding cakes. A teenager said she wanted to leave the city and felt guilty because the city had done nothing wrong. Two sisters arrived together, disagreed about nearly everything, and left carrying opposite ends of the same heavy bag.

At the end of the month, Mara’s supervisor asked for measurable outcomes.

She submitted:

*One drain repaired.*  
*Eleven people stayed longer than they intended.*  
*One person returned to apologize to someone who wasn’t here.*

Her supervisor asked whether she could put that in a spreadsheet.

She could.

By winter, there was a proposal to eliminate her position. At the budget meeting, the council asked what exactly the city received for her salary.

Mara had prepared an answer, but before she could give it, the man with the motorcycle helmet stood up in the public gallery.

He hadn’t brought the helmet this time.

“I don’t know how to explain it,” he said.

The council chair glanced at the clock, then back at him.

“Take your time.”

Mara put her notes away.
